status_summary: Steps align with two of the three examples. Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) created Workforce Pell Grants for short-term training, ED's final rule was published 2026-05-19, and the first program was approved in Iowa (release last reviewed 2026-08-04); the same law added a school-choice scholarship tax credit that states must opt into, with IRS proposed regulations published 2026-10-02 (see c11-09). Executive Order 14278 seeks 1 million new apprentices through Registered Apprenticeship, but industry-recognized apprenticeships remain unrevived and the registered-apprenticeship rule is not final (see c18-08). No loan product that replaces student loans was found; Workforce Pell is a grant, so its fit as a student-loan alternative is a partial match.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14278, Preparing Americans for High-Paying Skilled Trade Jobs of the Future, signed (published 2025-04-28): orders a plan to reach 1 million new active apprentices, including by extending Registered Apprenticeship to new industries.
DOL proposes to rescind affirmative action program requirements in the Registered Apprenticeship equal-opportunity rules.

Public Law 119-21 is signed. Section 83002 creates Workforce Pell Grants for short-term programs (150 to under 600 clock hours over 8 to under 15 weeks) from 2026-07-01, and section 70411 adds a federal tax credit for individual contributions to scholarship granting organizations that fund K-12 scholarships.
ED publishes the proposed Workforce Pell rule.

ED publishes the final Workforce Pell rule (91 FR 29254, effective 2026-07-20 with two instructions effective on publication); ED's release of 2026-05-18 says students can receive grants from 2026-07-01 and that governors, with state workforce boards, choose the qualifying fields.
ED announces approval of the first Workforce Pell program, a 14-week emergency medical technician program at Iowa Central Community College (release undated; its last-reviewed date is used).
DOL's regulatory agenda lists the registered apprenticeship nondiscrimination rule at the final rule stage; no final rule had appeared in the Federal Register as of 2026-10-07 per c18-08.

IRS proposes regulations for the section 25F scholarship credit (comments due 2026-12-01, hearing 2026-12-15); the credit applies to taxable years ending after 2026-12-31 and each state must elect to take part.

title: Promote education and training outside public schools and universities
uncertainties: Stage derivation: c18-08 is proposed 15 and c11-09 (school choice) is in_progress 40. Because the loan-alternative element is covered by the Workforce Pell grant (enacted, rule final, first program approved) that no chapter record tracks, the combined stage is in_progress 40. Workforce Pell is not a loan; whether it counts as a student-loan alternative as the Mandate means is a judgment, hence the partial match. Public law number 119-21 and sections 83002 and 70411 were confirmed on govinfo.gov. The Iowa approval release is undated; its last-reviewed date of 2026-08-04 is used. The source for the 2026-07-01 start of Workforce Pell grants is ED's release of 2026-05-18, which has no printed date and says the rule was on public inspection that day. The second Workforce Pell rule (student tuition, published 2026-07-01) and state certification notices were not read. c11-08 (loan caps and repayment) covers borrowing limits, not alternatives to loans, so no restated record tracks the loan-alternative element. DOL grants for apprenticeships mentioned in c18-08 are a news-reported item and were not used here.
